content:
Apple is expected to launch several brand-new Mac models later this year, including the first MacBook with a touch screen, the first Macs powered by the M6 chip, and more. Here's everything we know so far about the upcoming Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be the first Mac to feature a touch screen. Whether this new machine will be called the MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains to be seen, but it will represent the most significant redesign of the MacBook Pro in years.

Apple is reportedly testing macOS 27.1 on its high-end MacBook models, with a release expected in late October.

This all-new MacBook will be Apple's first product to feature both a touch screen and an OLED display. The current notch design is also expected to be removed in favour of a hole-punch cutout similar to the Dynamic Island on the iPhone. According to Bloomberg, this new high-end MacBook will be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the all-new touch-screen MacBook will feature the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the current MacBook Pro.

M6 MacBook

Apple is reportedly planning to launch its first Mac with the M6 chip later this year. The company is working on an updated entry-level MacBook Pro featuring the next-generation M6 processor.

According to reports, the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth, along with improvements in CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new entry-level MacBook Pro is not expected to feature any other changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, when it upgraded the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is currently working on the next-generation iMac update, which is reportedly set to launch this autumn.

The new iMac is expected to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. There are also rumours that the new iMac will offer new colour options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (TBD)

Lastly, Apple is also working on updates to the Mac mini and Mac Studio, but the release timeline for these models remains unclear.

As for the Mac mini, Apple is reportedly testing a new product line featuring both the M5 Pro and an entry-level M6 chip. Meanwhile, the Mac Studio is being tested with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processor variants.

According to Bloomberg, the launch timing for these models remains uncertain, depending on the "supply situation of memory chips." Most people expect the new Mac Studio to launch before the end of the year, but that now appears to be up in the air.

For reference, the current Mac mini is available with M4 and M4 Pro options, while the Mac Studio comes with M4 Max and M3 Ultra configurations.

Summary

Apple's current Mac lineup is in a rather awkward position, affected by supply tightness of memory and storage chips across the industry. Nevertheless, the company still has a strong slate of new models ready to go. What are your thoughts on the new Macs coming later this year? What do you think the MacBook Ultra will be priced at? Let us know in the comments section.
